bugLogs.title: Insufficient color contrast for stock status text and Add to Cart button
affected_users: older adults with declining contrast sensitivity
steps_to_reproduce: Observe the stock status paragraph and the Add to Cart button
Use a contrast checker or axe-core to evaluate color contrast
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Text and button label colors must have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against their background (or 3:1 for large text).
bugLogs.actual_behavior: Stock status paragraph has a contrast ratio of 1.6:1 (foreground #cccccc on #ffffff). Add to Cart button label has a contrast ratio of 2.93:1 (foreground #ffffff on #ff6600). Both fall below the required 4.5:1 ratio.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: In the CSS rule for p, change color from #cccccc to #767676 (4.54:1 on #ffffff; measured 1.6:1, required 4.5:1).

bugLogs.title: Product image missing alternative text
affected_users: users on slow connections who disable images
steps_to_reproduce: Locate the main product image displayed
Inspect the element in the DOM
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The element must have a descriptive alt attribute (or be marked as decorative with alt="" or role="presentation") so that screen readers can convey its purpose.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The element has no alt attribute, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no title, and no role override, leaving it without a text alternative.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add a meaningful alt attribute describing the product, e.g., . If the image is purely decorative, use alt="" or role="presentation".

bugLogs.title: Missing label for quantity input field
steps_to_reproduce: Attempt to focus the input using a screen reader or keyboard
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Each form control must have an associated label that is programmatically determinable, either via a <label> element, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or placeholder that serves as a persistent label.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The <input type="number" ...> element has no associated <label>, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no title attribute, and no placeholder, resulting in no accessible name.
bugLogs.suggested_fix:
Add a visible <label> element linked to the input via the 'for' attribute and give the input a matching 'id'. Example:

<label for="quantity">Quantity</label>
<input id="quantity" type="number" value="1" min="1" max="10" style="width: 50px;" aria-required="true">
